brief: NVIDIA shares fell over 4.3% on Thursday, pulling the Nasdaq down about 0.4% and pressuring Taiwan and South Korea tech markets, after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO following reports he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO; Harvey C. Jones becomes board chair while the board searches for a permanent CEO. UBS reads this as evidence that key-person and governance risk now matters alongside earnings growth, since AI equity gains have concentrated in a narrow group of companies. Investors are shifting from rewarding AI spending commitments to assessing monetization, balance sheets, utilization and returns, even as UBS says underlying demand stays robust (accelerating cloud revenue, forecast AI capex of USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027). Separately, UBS believes US restrictions on advanced AI-chip shipments to China are unlikely to ease and deployment scrutiny could rise, which could hurt overseas sales without denting underlying demand given tight compute supply. UBS keeps its structural AI conviction but argues for more selectivity: favoring strong hyperscalers, selective quality semis/hardware names, and broader diversification.
